_doc: Ruby. self_word: a bare identifier inside a class or module is also self.name (a method of the superclass, of an included module or of the host class that a module calls) unless a parameter, a block parameter, an assignment or a rescue variable of the method binds it (@local). name_map: A::B is A.B, a symbol :x is the name x. ref_cmd and path_sub: require 'a/b' includes a/b.rb (require_relative and load too; a name with an extension keeps it). protocol: methods that the language or a library calls by name (initialize, to_s, each, call, method_missing ...). path_roots: Rails calls the controllers, helpers, jobs, mailers, channels, migrations, initializers and rake tasks by convention (hard), models by name (an association symbol, autoload: the class is soft), models, views and services by their methods in templates (soft).
